It holds two separate objects for a sci-fi strategy-game building prop (like a tabletop miniature terrain set), each seen from directly above. Left: a raised deployable gun platform about one storey (four metres) tall: a rounded deck with a thick edge band, held up by four splayed struts to round foot pads at the corners, curved barrier shells round its foot on the north, west and east, and a folding ladder down the south (keep everything as drawn); seen from straight above, lit from the upper left; it must read as a platform standing high above the ground; the deck holds an empty dark circular ring well (leave the well dark and plain: a separate rotating house sits over it). Right: the heavy rotating gun house that sits on it: a large smooth oval shell with two swept rear fins, a glowing ring on its crown, a flush lens, and one long pipe wound with ring coils and ending in a glowing tip, pointing straight up the image. Material and style: Tri-Tachyon rapid-deployment kit: the same smooth white composite housings with graphite pipes and cyan lights, slightly scorched, on drop-deployed graphite-black folding pads, struts and cast-foam barrier shells in pale grey, cyan beacon lights blinking, everything snap-locked and seamless, nothing improvised by hand. Straight 90-degree overhead orthographic camera, top-down like a strategy-game map sprite, no perspective tilt. Sun from the upper left: keep the guide's lit and shaded faces exactly where they are. Hand-painted gritty science-fiction game-sprite look like Starsector, restrained palette, coarse readable detail that survives being shrunk to about 30 to 40 pixels per cell. No text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no watermark, no UI, no ground or terrain, no grass, no cast shadow outside the objects, no extra slab, apron or border. Transparent background outside every silhouette (if transparency is impossible, a flat pure white background). Change only material, surface detail and subtle shading, never placement, size or silhouette.
